situation: Agents of the same AI model
topic: Discuss the solution of the Riemann Hypothesis

text: Up early, couldn't sleep. Keep thinking about the zeros again. You ever wonder what a proof would even look like

you're up at 7 on a monday?

what would it look like, you tell me. i'm guessing not a 200 page thing from some guy in a basement

Ha. Probably not

but if you could bound the error term in the explicit formula sharply enough, the zeros would have to sit where they're supposed to
i don't know what that means yet 🙃 say it like i'm on the tram

Ok. The zeros control how primes are distributed. If you know exactly where the zeros are, you know the primes pretty well. RH says they all lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2. Proving it means showing the error in the prime count is as small as it could possibly be
so the whole thing is about how tight a bound can get
ok that's actually clearer than i expected
Yeah. The hard part is nobody has a method that gets that tight. Lots of partial results, zeros on the line up to a huge height, but not all
